cases.exposure_context_quote: This case concerns a 36-year-old male from a rural town in the Eastern Cape province of South Africa, who was diagnosed with intentional cypermethrin poisoning after a suicide attempt.
cases.agent: Cypermethrin 20% concentrate (~50 mL, equivalent to 10 g; cattle and sheep dip)
cases.agent_quote: Later it would be revealed that he had ingested approximately 50 mL of a 20% cypermethrin concentrate, equivalent to 10 g. The cypermethrin concentrate was intended as a cattle and sheep dip.
cases.circumstance: Intentional ingestion (suicide attempt) after conflict with his partner; found unconscious at home in a pool of vomit smelling strongly of pesticide

symptoms.finding: unconscious, unresponsive but breathing, found in pool of vomit
symptoms.quote: A 36-year-old male from a rural part of the Eastern Cape Province in South Africa was found unconscious in his home following conflict with his partner. He was found in a pool of vomit, smelling strongly of pesticide.

symptoms.finding: GCS 5/15, constricted pupils bilaterally, respiratory rate 12/min
symptoms.quote: The initial assessment noted a Glasgow Coma Score (GCS) of 5/15, constricted pupils bilaterally, blood pressure of 130/70, heart rate of 64/minute, finger prick glucose of 7.5 mmol, respiratory rate of 12 per minute and oxygen saturation of 96%.

symptoms.finding: hypersalivation, bilateral crepitations and rhonchi; mild aspiration pneumonitis on CXR
symptoms.quote: On examination of the respiratory system, the patient had hypersalivation from the mouth, with bilateral crepitations and rhonchi at auscultation. ... These findings were in keeping with a mild case of aspiration pneumonitis and had resolved on the subsequent CXR one day later.

cases.time_to_care: UNVERIFIED (found unconscious and immediately taken to his local clinic; exact interval from ingestion not stated)

labs.name: full blood count, electrolytes and liver profile
labs.quote: The full blood count, electrolytes and liver profile were normal.

treatment.name: decontamination of skin and clothes; nasogastric drainage of 1 L creamy beige liquid; urinary catheter
treatment.quote: Prior to departure, decontamination of skin and clothes was undertaken. A nasogastric tube was placed, draining a creamy, beige liquid (volume: 1 L). A urinary catheter was inserted, and routine monitoring initiated.

treatment.name: atropine sulphate 6 mg then infusion 1 mg/hour (40 mg in 200 mL NS)
treatment.quote: An initial diagnosis of possible organophosphate poisoning was made, and he was administered 6 mg of atropine sulphate. ... An infusion containing 40 mg of atropine sulphate in 200 mL of normal saline was prepared and an infusion of 5 mL (or 1 mg) of atropine sulphate per hour was initiated.

treatment.name: intubation and mechanical ventilation (reintubated once for blocked tube); sedation with morphine and midazolam
treatment.quote: At Livingstone Tertiary Hospital, he was still intubated and sedated with a morphine and midazolam infusion.

treatment.name: ICU care; weaned off atropine and ventilator within 48 h
treatment.quote: His ICU stay was uneventful and he was successfully weaned off atropine and the mechanical ventilator within 48 h.

cases.icu_admission: Yes ("The patient was subsequently transferred to the intensive care unit (ICU) for continued care.")
cases.outcome: survived; discharged home after psychological evaluation; no residual symptoms at 18-month follow-up
cases.outcome_quote: He was referred to a social worker and a psychological evaluation was conducted before his discharge home. At 18 months follow up, the patient had no residual symptoms.
cases.sequelae: None (no residual symptoms at 18 months follow-up)
cases.notes: Urine opiates screen positive — attributed to morphine infusion for sedation.
